issues.description: The problem statement's UML names the boolean attribute in ExcellenceLand as 'excellentEnough' (problem_statement.md, lines 35-36). The solution implementation instead uses a boolean field named 'isExcellent' with a getter isExcellent() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java, lines 7-23). This name mismatch between the specified attribute and the solution can confuse students about which attribute name and getter to implement and may cause automated tests that expect 'excellentEnough' (and its corresponding getter) to fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the attribute name consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution to use the UML name: change the boolean field to 'excellentEnough', accept 'excellentEnough' as the constructor parameter, and provide a public getter (e.g. isExcellentEnough() or getExcellentEnough()). Or update the problem statement/UML to name the boolean 'isExcellent' and indicate the corresponding getter is isExcellent(), so all artifacts use the same identifier.
